items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: And Paul Barberin one night, he had a chick, man, in Philadelphia. I went and bought it with some rope.

ctx.x: Then he come looking for me. Ain't nobody been here, I got to slip all around, went all around, got over some fences, they get in the back house, man, because of the shoppers that I was going to steal. People leave the back door for now, you know. But he still believes it was me. But I, but he never did find out it was me. And Paul Barberin one night, he had a chick, man, in Philadelphia. I went and bought it with some rope. And like my room is over there, when you look in this window, I run the rope all through…

items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: I say they ain't got no band, but they sure it's got some good rhythm. I say I'll meet Paul Boblin.

ctx.x: See? I never say it's great.

So people tell me, how do you like it? I say I don't like playing solos. Which I don't. I like that this time I play rhythm behind the other guy that ain't blowing. And if you play that correct rhythm behind the guy that's blowing, you get much credit as the man playing that melody. See? Because we're just like when we went to Rose in the Bar Room. We didn't have much of a band. I say they ain't got no band, but they sure it's got some good rhythm. I say I'll meet Paul Boblin. That was a great... And a guy, he's…
Oh sure. That's a great thing.
